prompt.body: 90s hard rock at 128 BPM in B minor. The song is about an affair in a '97 Civic. Slash's Les Paul, but played clean with just enough grit — the slowest, most sensual track on the album. The vocalist is Axl Rose circa 1991 — breathy in the verse, wailing on the held notes, screaming on the chorus. The drummer plays a half-time backbeat with brushes on the verse (sleazy, late-night) and opens up to a full double-kick backbeat on the chorus. The bass is fat, walking, almost R&B. The chorus is a gang-shout but lower-register, slinkier. Slash-style solo with one long slow bend and a mournful pull-up at the end. No piano, no synth, no ballad-section piano. The lyrics are about a Marine's girlfriend, a tape deck that ate the singer's best mixes, the lights of the city, the room underwater. Think Whitesnake 'Here I Go Again' or GnR 'Patience' — but darker, more desperate. The song is sensual and doomed. The singer knows he's destroying her and he does it anyway. Production: dry, late-night, the bass is the lead voice. FIRE.
